_comment: Facility dossiers for the town map. One per energy subsector. Layers: IT (corporate), OT (control systems), PIT (Platform IT: computing embedded inside the physical asset itself; the term comes from US DoD usage). 'background_cases' are historical incidents from the model's general knowledge as of its training cutoff, given with year and a pointer; they are NOT from the allowlisted feeds and must be checked against the Where-to-look sources before being cited. 'live_match' lists keywords used to pull this week's board items into the dossier.

layer_definitions.IT: Corporate information technology: email, ERP, billing, customer portals, engineering file shares, Active Directory, VPNs, cloud. Breaches here are business problems.
layer_definitions.OT: Operational technology: the systems that monitor and control the physical process. SCADA servers, HMIs, historians, engineering workstations, PLCs, RTUs, DCS. Breaches here can change physical state.
layer_definitions.PIT: Platform IT: computing embedded inside the asset itself: protective relays, turbine governors, inverter firmware, smart-meter chips, pipeline leak-detection units, reactor protection logic. Hardest to patch, longest-lived, often vendor-controlled.

purdue: Level 3 site operations (engineering workstations, historians, domain services)
Level 3.5 DMZ (jump hosts, patch servers, data diodes)
breach_pattern: 1. Reconnaissance: public filings, vendor press releases, job ads naming the SCADA product, Shodan for exposed HMIs and VPNs.
2. Initial access: phishing into corporate IT; a VPN or firewall flaw; stolen credentials from a contractor; a vendor's remote-access tool; an internet-exposed controller.
3. Foothold and credential theft: domain admin in IT, or a harvested engineering account.
4. Crossing to OT: through a flat network, a dual-homed engineering workstation, a shared jump host, or the same vendor remote-access path used for maintenance.
5. Learning the process: reading HMI screens, historian data and PLC logic to understand what each tag does. This can take months (Ukraine 2015 took about six).
6. Effect: ransomware on IT that forces a precautionary OT shutdown (Colonial 2021); or direct OT manipulation: setpoint changes, breaker trips, safety-system tampering, firmware wipes.
7. Persistence or destruction: living-off-the-land for prepositioning (Volt Typhoon), or wipers to slow recovery (Ukraine 2016, 2022).
attack_types: ransomware on IT with OT shutdown as collateral
supply-chain compromise via vendor or integrator
data theft of grid topology and engineering drawings

facilities.name: Nuclear plant

variables.typical_ot_impact: OT reached, no process effect (safety systems are isolated by design)
variables.asset_type: reactor protection system, plant process computer, digital I&C

IT: engineering document management (drawings are high-value to adversaries)
OT: plant process computer and DCS
digital instrumentation and control for non-safety systems
physical security and access control systems
PIT: reactor protection system logic (often analog or hard-wired by design)
turbine control and generator protection relays

OT: legacy Windows on plant computers
vendor laptops during outages
flat networks in balance-of-plant systems
PIT: decades-old firmware with no update path

attacks: removable-media malware reaching plant networks (Davis-Besse Slammer 2003, Gundremmingen 2016)
information operations about radiation (Ukraine alert app, this week)
facilities.how_breach: Almost never through the safety system. The path is corporate IT, then balance-of-plant OT or the physical-security network, through contractor laptops and USB media during refuelling outages. The effect is operational disruption and stolen engineering data, not reactor control.

background_cases.case: Davis-Besse (US): Slammer worm reached the plant process computer via a contractor connection; the plant was offline for other reasons.

anatomy.bypass: A contractor's network link bypassed the plant firewall
anatomy.mechanics: SQL Slammer worm traffic saturated the network; the safety parameter display system was unavailable for hours
process: Worm enters via contractor connection
Network saturation
Plant computer unavailable; plant was already offline
next_layers: Inventory and control every third-party connection
Network segmentation that does not rely on a single perimeter

background_cases.case: Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power: data theft and leak of plant documents, attributed by South Korea to North Korea.
Kudankulam (India): DTrack malware on the administrative network, confirmed by NPCIL.

facilities.name: Thermal power plant

variables.regulatory_trigger: NERC CIP-002 to CIP-015 for BES assets
variables.asset_type: DCS, turbine controls, emissions monitoring, fuel handling

IT: corporate IT, fuel procurement, market bidding systems
OT: distributed control system (DCS)
burner management and boiler safety systems
historian and engineering workstations
safety instrumented systems reachable from DCS
unpatched engineering workstations
PIT: governor firmware updates only via vendor

attacks: safety-system tampering (Triton 2017 was a petrochemical plant; the same SIS products run in power plants)
ransomware on IT forcing precautionary shutdowns
facilities.how_breach: Through the vendor. OEMs hold remote connections for turbine monitoring; a compromised OEM account or a flat DMZ lets an attacker reach the DCS. Triton shows the next step: a dual-homed engineering workstation reaching the safety controller.

background_cases.case: Triton/Trisis: attackers reached Triconex safety controllers at a Saudi petrochemical plant via an engineering workstation; a plant trip revealed them.
background_cases.check: Mandiant and Dragos reports; Schneider Electric advisory

anatomy.attribution: TEMP.Veles, linked by Mandiant to a Russian government research institute (TsNIIKhM), sanctioned by the US Treasury in 2020; high in the public record
anatomy.bypass: IT compromise, then a dual-homed engineering workstation that could reach the Triconex safety controllers; the controllers' physical key switch was left in Program mode
anatomy.mechanics: Custom TriStation protocol implementation to upload a malicious logic payload into the safety controller's memory; a bug in the payload caused a failed validation and a safe shutdown, which exposed the operation
process: Gain IT access and move to the OT DMZ
Compromise the SIS engineering workstation
Reverse-engineer TriStation; build an implant
Upload to controllers in Program mode
Trip reveals the intrusion; investigation finds the implant
next_layers: Physical key switch policy and alarms for Program mode
No dual-homed workstations between DCS and SIS; separate SIS engineering
Monitor TriStation and other engineering protocols
Integrity checks on safety-controller logic

background_cases.case: Industroyer2 at a Ukrainian electricity provider, aimed at substations feeding generation and load; blocked, per CERT-UA and ESET.

facilities.name: Substation

variables.regulatory_trigger: NERC CIP-005 (electronic security perimeter), CIP-007, CIP-010; FERC Order 887 (INSM)
variables.asset_type: protective relays (IEDs), RTUs, bay controllers, SCADA gateway

OT: SCADA master and HMI at the control centre
substation gateway / RTU, IEC 61850 station bus, DNP3 links
PIT: breaker and transformer controllers, IEC 61850 GOOSE messaging

OT: cellular and serial links without authentication (DNP3 pre-secure-auth)
exposed engineering ports on gateways
shared vendor remote access
PIT: relay settings changed via engineering software
GOOSE spoofing on the station bus

attacks: configuration and credential theft from network gear (Zyxel this week)
facilities.how_breach: Phish the utility, steal VPN credentials, reach the control-centre SCADA network through a weak DMZ, learn the HMI, then either operate breakers from the HMI or speak the grid protocols directly to the substation gateways. Wipers on the SCADA servers and a telephony DDoS on the call centre slow the recovery.

background_cases.case: Ukraine, December 23: BlackEnergy intrusion, remote HMI operation opened breakers at three distribution companies, ~225,000 customers for up to six hours; KillDisk and a call-centre DDoS followed.
background_cases.check: SANS/E-ISAC 'Analysis of the Cyber Attack on the Ukrainian Power Grid' (2016); CISA alert IR-ALERT-H-16-056-01

anatomy.attribution: Sandworm (GRU Unit 74455), per US DOJ indictment (2020) and multiple governments; confidence high in the public record
anatomy.bypass: Spear-phishing with macro documents delivered BlackEnergy 3 to corporate IT; VPN credentials harvested; the VPNs to the SCADA network had no MFA
anatomy.mechanics: Months of reconnaissance inside the networks; operators watched their own cursors move as attackers used remote-desktop sessions to open breakers at the HMI; KillDisk wiped workstations and serial-to-Ethernet converter firmware was corrupted; a telephony DDoS flooded the call centre
process: Phish → BlackEnergy → credentials
Pivot via VPN to the SCADA network (no MFA)
Six months learning the HMI and the field
Remote HMI operation opens breakers at ~30 substations
KillDisk and firmware corruption to delay recovery; UPS and call centre attacked
Manual restoration within hours; automation lost for months
next_layers: MFA on every remote path into OT
Separate corporate identity from OT identity
Alert on interactive sessions to HMIs outside maintenance windows
Keep the ability to operate manually and test it
Protect serial converters and firmware integrity; offline backups of engineering files

background_cases.case: Industroyer/CrashOverride at a Kyiv transmission substation: malware speaking IEC 101/104, 61850 and OPC natively; about an hour of outage.

anatomy.attribution: Sandworm, per ESET, Dragos and later US indictment; high in the public record
anatomy.bypass: Rather than driving the HMI, the malware spoke the grid protocols (IEC 101, IEC 104, IEC 61850, OPC DA) directly to substation devices, so it did not need an operator session
anatomy.mechanics: Modular framework: a backdoor, a launcher, four protocol payloads, a wiper, and a denial-of-service exploit against a Siemens SIPROTEC relay; it de-energised a transmission substation for about an hour
process: Initial access (not fully public)
Deploy framework on a control-network host
Map device addresses
Issue protocol commands to open breakers
Wiper to slow recovery; relay DoS to block protection
next_layers: Protocol-aware monitoring on the station bus (detect IEC 104/61850 commands from unexpected hosts)
Allow-lists of which hosts may speak control protocols
Patch and segment protection relays; FERC Order 887's internal network monitoring is this lesson in rule form

background_cases.case: Volt Typhoon: CISA, NSA and FBI advisory on PRC state actors prepositioning in US critical infrastructure including energy, using living-off-the-land techniques.

anatomy.attribution: PRC state-sponsored, per CISA/NSA/FBI with Five Eyes partners (AA24-038A); high
anatomy.bypass: Exploitation of internet-facing devices (routers, VPN appliances, firewalls) and use of valid credentials; living-off-the-land so that no malware triggers alarms
anatomy.mechanics: Access through end-of-life SOHO routers and edge devices; credential theft from Active Directory; command-line tools native to Windows; dormant presence for years in utilities, pipelines, water and communications
process: Compromise edge devices and build a proxy network of hijacked routers
Enter victim networks with valid credentials
Move to OT-adjacent assets; collect information on OT
Maintain access for a crisis; no disruptive action observed
next_layers: Patch or replace edge devices; retire end-of-life routers
Logging sufficient to see LOTL behaviour (command-line auditing, PowerShell logging)
Credential hygiene, tiered admin, MFA
Hunt rather than wait: the advisory's indicators and techniques

facilities.name: Wind and solar farm

variables.regulatory_trigger: NERC CIP applies only above BES thresholds; most DER sits outside it; IEEE 1547, UL 2941 emerging
variables.asset_type: inverters, turbine controllers, plant SCADA, cloud monitoring portals

IT: cloud monitoring and fleet-management portals (often vendor-hosted abroad)
OT: plant controller and SCADA, power-plant controller for grid codes
satellite or cellular links to remote sites

IT: mass remote control through a vendor cloud (thousands of inverters behind one account)
OT: satellite modem flaws (Viasat 2022 affected German wind turbines)
unauthenticated Modbus TCP on plant networks
PIT: inverter firmware flaws disclosed by researchers (SUN:DOWN 2025)
foreign-made cellular radios inside inverters, a 2025 policy concern

attacks: fleet-wide curtailment via a compromised vendor cloud
collateral loss of monitoring from satellite attacks
hacktivist defacement of solar monitoring HMIs
supply-chain hardware concerns driving the foreign grid-component ban (this week)
facilities.how_breach: Not through the farm, through the cloud. One phished installer or vendor account can address thousands of inverters at once. The physical effect is curtailment or disconnection in bulk, which matters to the grid when solar supplies a large share of daytime load.

background_cases.case: Viasat KA-SAT attack on the day of the Ukraine invasion knocked out remote monitoring of ~5,800 Enercon wind turbines in Germany.

anatomy.attribution: Russian military intelligence (GRU), per EU, UK and US statements (2022); high
anatomy.bypass: A misconfigured VPN appliance gave access to the satellite network's management segment; from there, 'AcidRain' wiper commands were pushed to modems
anatomy.mechanics: Management-network access used to issue a destructive firmware update to tens of thousands of modems at the start of the invasion; collateral loss of monitoring for ~5,800 German wind turbines
process: Exploit VPN misconfiguration
Reach the management network
Push wiper to modems in bulk
Effect: loss of connectivity and remote monitoring across Europe
next_layers: Do not depend on one link for OT telemetry; second path (cellular, leased line)
Harden the provider's management plane: it is your attack surface too
Know which remote assets go blind if a carrier fails, and how long you can run blind

background_cases.case: Hacktivists (allegedly Arab-linked) tampered with Japanese solar monitoring devices (Contec SolarView) to steal bank credentials, per Japanese reports.
Forescout SUN:DOWN research disclosed dozens of flaws in Sungrow, Growatt and SMA inverter ecosystems enabling fleet takeover.
background_cases.check: Forescout Vedere Labs report; CISA ICS advisories

facilities.name: Upstream oil and gas

variables.regulatory_trigger: largely voluntary in the US (API 1164 for pipelines does not apply); TSA directives cover pipelines, not wells
variables.asset_type: wellhead RTUs, drilling control systems, SCADA over cellular

IT: seismic and reservoir data (very high value)
OT: drilling control and dynamic positioning on rigs
wellhead and gathering SCADA over cellular and satellite
PIT: wellhead safety valves and shutdown panels

OT: remote sites with exposed cellular routers
rig networks with vendor VPNs
PIT: proprietary tools updated only by the OEM

facilities.how_breach: Through the services firm. Exploration companies outsource drilling, logging and completion; a ransomware hit on the contractor freezes operations across many operators at once, as Halliburton's 2024 incident showed.

background_cases.case: Night Dragon: espionage campaign against oil and gas majors for bid and production data, attributed by McAfee to China-based actors.
Halliburton ransomware (August): systems taken offline, roughly $35 million impact disclosed in SEC filings; RansomHub claimed it.

anatomy.attribution: RansomHub (criminal RaaS) claimed; company did not name; moderate
anatomy.mechanics: Ransomware on IT; systems taken offline proactively; ~$35M impact in filings
process: Initial access (not public)
Ransomware deployment
Proactive shutdown of systems
Customer operations affected through the services dependency
next_layers: For operators: map dependence on oilfield-services contractors' IT
Contract terms for incident notification and continuity
Segmentation between contractor networks and your own

facilities.name: Pipeline compressor station

variables.regulatory_trigger: TSA Security Directives Pipeline-2021-01/02 series (post-Colonial); proposed rule under 49 CFR; PHMSA
variables.typical_ot_impact: OT process affected or precautionary shutdown
variables.asset_type: pipeline SCADA, compressor controls, leak detection, metering

IT: billing and nomination systems (what Colonial actually lost)
OT: pipeline SCADA with thousands of miles of RTUs
compressor station PLCs and turbine controls
leak-detection systems
PIT: valve actuators and emergency shutdown logic

IT: a single unused VPN account without MFA (Colonial)
billing dependence: no billing, no shipping
OT: SCADA reachable from IT for scheduling data
long-lived vendor remote access to compressor stations

attacks: ransomware on IT causing a precautionary OT shutdown (Colonial 2021)
ransomware on a compressor facility's OT after IT crossover (CISA 2020 advisory)
facilities.how_breach: Colonial's path is the template: a leaked password for a VPN account that had no multi-factor authentication, DarkSide ransomware on corporate IT, and a decision to shut the pipeline because billing and safety visibility were in doubt. OT was not touched; fuel still stopped for six days.

background_cases.case: CISA alert AA20-049A: ransomware entered a natural-gas compression facility via a phishing link, crossed from IT to OT, and encrypted HMIs; two-day shutdown.
Colonial Pipeline, May 7: DarkSide ransomware on IT via a VPN account without MFA; the 5,500-mile pipeline shut for six days; $4.4M ransom paid, part recovered by DOJ.
background_cases.check: Congressional testimony of CEO Joseph Blount (June 2021); DOJ seizure announcement

anatomy.attribution: DarkSide ransomware-as-a-service affiliates, criminal; FBI attribution; high
anatomy.bypass: A legacy VPN account, no longer in use but still active, with no multi-factor authentication, and a password that had appeared in a prior leak
anatomy.mechanics: Login via VPN, lateral movement in corporate IT, data theft (~100 GB) then DarkSide ransomware encryption; the company shut the pipeline itself because billing and the safety of operations could not be assured
process: Credential from a leak reused on the VPN (no MFA)
Access corporate IT; exfiltrate data
Deploy ransomware
Operator shuts OT as a precaution
Six-day fuel disruption on the US East Coast; $4.4M paid, ~$2.3M recovered by DOJ
next_layers: MFA everywhere; kill unused accounts
Know which IT systems OT depends on (billing, scheduling) and plan to run without them
Offline backups; tested restoration
TSA security directives made much of this mandatory for pipelines

facilities.name: Refinery and LNG terminal

variables.regulatory_trigger: CFATS lapsed in 2023 (US); Coast Guard MTSA cyber rules for terminals (2025); EU NIS2
variables.asset_type: DCS, safety instrumented systems, tank gauging, terminal automation

IT: trading, scheduling and terminal management systems
OT: DCS across process units
safety instrumented systems (SIS)
terminal automation and tank gauging

IT: ransomware with large cash incentives (Saudi Aramco contractors 2021)
OT: SIS engineering workstation on the same network as DCS (Triton)
internet-exposed tank-gauging devices (ATGs)
PIT: SIS key switch left in program mode

attacks: wipers on IT (Shamoon 2012 at Saudi Aramco, 35,000 machines)
ransomware and extortion against majors and traders
facilities.how_breach: Triton's path: IT compromise, then a jump to a dual-homed engineering workstation that could reach the safety controllers, then custom code to reprogram the SIS. The attackers' mistake triggered a safe shutdown; a correct version could have disabled the last line of defence against explosion.

background_cases.case: Shamoon wiped ~35,000 Saudi Aramco workstations; production unaffected, business crippled for weeks.
background_cases.check: Saudi Aramco statements; US officials attributed to Iran

anatomy.attribution: Iran, per US officials; 'Cutting Sword of Justice' claimed; moderate-high
anatomy.bypass: Insider or phished credentials enabled network-wide deployment (details disputed)
anatomy.mechanics: Wiper overwrote the master boot record of ~35,000 workstations with an image; production unaffected because OT was separate, business crippled for weeks
process: Access to corporate domain
Mass deployment via domain tools
Overwrite boot records simultaneously
Weeks of manual recovery
next_layers: Domain hardening and tiered admin
Offline, immutable backups and rebuild capacity
Separation of OT from the corporate domain, which is what saved production

background_cases.case: Triton at a Saudi petrochemical plant: first malware built to attack a safety instrumented system; attributed by Mandiant to a Russian government research institute (TEMP.Veles).
background_cases.check: Mandiant/FireEye report (2018); US Treasury sanctions on TsNIIKhM (2020)

facilities.name: Battery storage site

variables.regulatory_trigger: NERC CIP only above BES thresholds; NFPA 855 for fire safety; state-level foreign-vendor rules emerging
variables.asset_type: battery management systems, power conversion systems, EMS

OT: energy management system dispatching the site
power conversion system controllers, site SCADA
PIT: battery management system firmware (cell balancing, thermal limits)

OT: EMS exposed for dispatch integrations
building-management-style controllers (the refrigeration pattern this week)
PIT: BMS limits changeable by firmware or configuration
foreign-manufactured BMS with undocumented remote paths

attacks: setpoint and thermal-limit manipulation (the European refrigeration attacks are the closest live analogue)
facilities.how_breach: Like the fridges this week: a vendor remote-access path or an exposed controller, then a changed setpoint. For a battery that means charge limits and thermal thresholds, where the failure mode is fire rather than spoiled food. No public BESS cyber incident has caused a fire; the vulnerability research exists.

background_cases.case: US House and state inquiries into Chinese-made BESS and inverter hardware with cellular radios; no confirmed attack, a supply-chain concern.
background_cases.check: Congressional letters; Reuters reporting (May 2025) on undocumented communication devices in inverters

facilities.name: EV charging hub

variables.regulatory_trigger: NEVI program cyber requirements (US); UK smart-charging regulations; ISO 15118, OCPP

IT: charge-point management system (CPMS) in the cloud
OT: OCPP links between chargers and CPMS
site load-management controllers

IT: cloud CPMS as single point of control for thousands of chargers
OT: OCPP without TLS or with weak auth
load managers reachable on site networks
PIT: charger firmware flaws (Pwn2Own Automotive 2024-2026 found dozens)

attacks: mass load manipulation to stress distribution feeders (demonstrated in research, not yet observed)
hacktivist defacement of charger screens (Russia 2022, Isle of Wight 2022)
facilities.how_breach: Through the cloud again: one CPMS account can start or stop charging across a region. Research shows synchronized switching of large charger fleets could destabilize local distribution; the observed attacks so far are defacements and fraud.

background_cases.case: Chargers in Russia displayed pro-Ukraine messages after a Ukrainian supplier's component was repurposed; Isle of Wight chargers showed pornography after a compromise.
Pwn2Own Automotive (Tokyo) researchers exploited multiple commercial EV chargers (ChargePoint, Autel, JuiceBox among them).

facilities.name: Data centre

variables.subsector: data centres, the fastest-growing firm load
variables.value_chain: consumption at utility scale; often with on-site generation
variables.regulatory_trigger: NERC CIP only if registered as a large load or generator; state interconnection rules; EU NIS2 (digital infrastructure)
variables.asset_type: building management, cooling controllers, UPS and switchgear, backup generation, GPU clusters

IT: tenant and cloud workloads, the AI models themselves
OT: building management and cooling control (the refrigeration class attacked in Europe this week)
power distribution: switchgear, UPS controllers, generator controls
physical access control

IT: AI-agent and supply-chain compromises (WorkOS/ARTEX, cPGuard this week)
OT: internet-reachable BMS and cooling controllers
vendor remote access for cooling and power maintenance
PIT: BMC flaws across fleets of identical servers

attacks: physical intrusions aided by access-control compromise
facilities.how_breach: Two routes: through the building (BMS and cooling vendors, the same path as the European refrigeration cases) or through the tenants (a cloud or AI workload compromise that reaches management networks). The physical effect is thermal: a few minutes without cooling at AI rack densities is an outage.

background_cases.case: OVHcloud Strasbourg fire destroyed a data centre; not cyber, but the reference case for what loss of a site means to dependent services.
Research disclosures of BMC and DCIM flaws (e.g., CyberPower PowerPanel, Dataprobe iBoot PDU) enabling remote power control, reported by Trellix.

facilities.name: LNG terminal and tanker
facilities.subsector: energy transport: LNG and tanker shipping

variables.regulatory_trigger: US Coast Guard MTSA cyber rule (2025); IMO 2021 cyber-risk resolution; port-state controls
variables.typical_ot_impact: OT process affected (cargo, navigation, terminal automation)
variables.asset_type: terminal automation, cargo control, ECDIS/navigation, GPS, satellite links, port IT

IT: port community systems and booking (NotPetya hit Maersk's)
OT: terminal automation and loading arms
vessel cargo control, ballast, engine management
navigation: ECDIS, GPS/GNSS, AIS
vessel networks reachable via satellite link
terminal automation on vendor remote access
PIT: GNSS spoofing in conflict zones (Black Sea, Gulf, Baltic)

facilities.how_breach: Ports fall through IT: one ransomware event and the terminal stops loading. Ships fall through the link: a satellite terminal or a GNSS receiver, then the bridge. The energy effect is a delayed cargo, which in a tight LNG market is a price.

background_cases.case: NotPetya shut Maersk's global operations and port terminals for days; ~$300M impact reported.
Ransomware (LockBit attributed) halted Japan's Port of Nagoya container operations for about two days.

anatomy.mechanics: Ransomware on the port's unified terminal system; container operations halted for about two days
process: Initial access (not public)
Encrypt the terminal system
Operations stop; manual workarounds
Restore from backups
next_layers: Port community systems need the same continuity planning as SCADA
Backups tested for restoration time, not just existence

background_cases.case: Widespread GNSS interference in the Baltic and Black Sea affecting shipping and aviation, reported by national authorities.
background_cases.check: national aviation and maritime authority notices

facilities.name: Interconnector and subsea cable
facilities.subsector: energy transport: interconnectors and subsea cables

variables.subsector: cross-border power interconnectors; subsea power and data cables; satellite links that carry grid telemetry
variables.regulatory_trigger: ENTSO-E network codes; NERC CIP for US ties; national critical-infrastructure protection; UNCLOS for subsea
variables.typical_ot_impact: OT process affected or physical/safety impact
variables.asset_type: HVDC converter stations, cable landing stations, SCADA over leased lines and satellite

OT: HVDC converter control
landing-station SCADA and protection
telemetry over leased lines, microwave, satellite

IT: market-platform compromise affects flows across borders
OT: remote landing stations with thin staffing and vendor access
telemetry over satellite (Viasat 2022)
PIT: physical sabotage of cables (Baltic 2023-2025) outside cyber but inseparable in planning

attacks: physical cable damage with cyber follow-on uncertainty (Baltic incidents)
satellite telemetry loss (Viasat 2022 and wind turbines)
HVDC control compromise (no public case; research only)
facilities.how_breach: The cable itself is cut by an anchor; the cyber risk sits in the converter stations and in the links that carry their telemetry. Lose the satellite link and the operator loses view of a remote landing station; combine with a physical event and restoration slows.

background_cases.case: Viasat KA-SAT attack removed remote monitoring from thousands of wind turbines and other users across Europe.
background_cases.check: Viasat statement; EU and US attributions to Russia

anatomy.attribution: Russian military intelligence (GRU), per EU, UK and US statements (2022); high
anatomy.bypass: A misconfigured VPN appliance gave access to the satellite network's management segment; from there, 'AcidRain' wiper commands were pushed to modems
anatomy.mechanics: Management-network access used to issue a destructive firmware update to tens of thousands of modems at the start of the invasion; collateral loss of monitoring for ~5,800 German wind turbines

Reach the management network
Push wiper to modems in bulk
Effect: loss of connectivity and remote monitoring across Europe
next_layers: Do not depend on one link for OT telemetry; second path (cellular, leased line)

Know which remote assets go blind if a carrier fails, and how long you can run blind

background_cases.case: Balticconnector gas pipeline and a telecom cable damaged in the Gulf of Finland; Finnish investigation pointed to a ship's anchor.
Further Baltic subsea cable damage incidents (Estlink 2, C-Lion1) under investigation by Finland and partners.
background_cases.check: Finnish and Estonian authorities; NATO statements
